data.name: Shiphrah
data.gender_notes: Shiphrah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew shaphar, meaning 'to sing' or 'to shout for joy'. In the Bible, Shiphrah is the name of an Egyptian midwife who helped deliver the Hebrew babies during the time of the Israelites' enslavement. She is praised for her bravery and kindness in Exodus 1:15–16 and 2:16–17. The name Shiphrah carries the meaning “God is my song” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew. Parents who choose Shiphrah usually hope their child will grow to embody god is my song and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Shiphrah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God is my song.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shiphrah total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_greek.name: Σιφρα
in_greek.meaning: Σήμα απελευθέρωσης, φανερή πίστη, προστασία της βιολογίας
in_greek.long_meaning: Σήμα απελευθέρωσης και προστασίας από την πλανήτηση της φύσης. Η Σιφρα συμβολίζει τον καθορισμό του αίματος του Ιησού Χριστού και την προστασία από την πλανήτηση της φύσης. Εμφανίζεται στην Βίβλο ως ο τοπικός είσπρακτορας του Φαραώ κατά την είσπραξη των Ισραηλίων.

in_latin.name: Shiphrah
in_latin.meaning: Signum libertatis, fides manifesta, tutela naturae
in_latin.long_meaning: Signum libertatis et tutela naturae. Shiphrah indicat institutionem sanguinis Christi et tutelam a corruptione naturae. Inscriptus est in Biblia ut magistratus aegyptius qui tractus est per liberalem dispensationem de Israel.

in_english.name: Shiphrah
in_english.meaning: Sign of liberation, manifest faith, nature's protection
in_english.long_meaning: Sign of liberation and protection from the corruption of nature. Shiphrah signifies the institution of Christ's blood and protection from the corruption of nature. It is mentioned in the Bible as the Egyptian official who was treated with liberality regarding the Israelites.
